items.title: The Act, the Appointed Day & the Capital Question
items.body:
## Enactment

- The **Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014** was passed by Parliament and assented on **1 March 2014**; the **appointed day was 2 June 2014**, when **Telangana** was formed (s.3) and the residuary State retained the name **Andhra Pradesh** (s.4).
- Telangana got **10 districts**; AP kept the **Coastal Andhra + Rayalaseema** regions.
- A **common Governor** served both States for a period fixed by the President (s.7).

## Hyderabad & the new capital

- **Section 5:** **Hyderabad is the common capital for a period not exceeding 10 years**; thereafter it is Telangana's capital and AP must have a new capital.
- **Section 8:** the Governor has **special responsibility** for law & order and security in the common capital area (Greater Hyderabad).
- **Section 6:** the Centre set up an **expert committee (K.C. Sivaramakrishnan)** to study new-capital options within six months. AP later chose **Amaravati** (greenfield capital via land pooling).

## Political representation

| Body | Undivided AP | Andhra Pradesh | Telangana |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lok Sabha | 42 | 25 | 17 |
| Assembly | 294 | 175 | 119 |
keyPoints: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 assented 1 March 2014; appointed day = 2 June 2014 (Telangana formed).
Section 5: Hyderabad is the common capital for a period not exceeding 10 years.
Section 6 expert committee on the new capital was headed by K.C. Sivaramakrishnan.
AP chose Amaravati as its greenfield capital via land pooling.
Seats: AP got 25 Lok Sabha & 175 Assembly; Telangana 17 & 119 (of erstwhile 42 & 294).
items.mnemonic: '2-6-14' = 2 June 2014 appointed day; capital clock runs 10 years to June 2024.

items.title: Division of Assets, Liabilities, Institutions & Employees
items.body:
## Assets and liabilities

- General/movable assets, cash balances and funds were apportioned mainly on the **population-ratio basis** (~58:42, AP:Telangana); **immovable assets pass to the State where they are located**.
- The **Ninth Schedule** lists **government companies and corporations** (s.68/71) to be divided; the **Tenth Schedule** lists **state institutions whose facilities continue** for both States (s.75).

## Employees

- Allocation of the erstwhile State's employees between AP and Telangana was guided by the **Kamalanathan Committee**; 'nativity/local cadre' disputes were a major post-bifurcation friction point.

## Fiscal transition (Section 46)

- The **Thirteenth Finance Commission** award was apportioned between the successor States; the President referred the matter to the **Fourteenth Finance Commission** for **separate awards**.
- The Centre was to consider a **special development package** with incentives, **particularly for Rayalaseema and the north-coastal regions** (s.46(2)-(3)).
- The 14th FC recommended a **revenue-deficit grant** to bridge AP's post-bifurcation resource gap.
keyPoints: Assets split mainly by population ratio (~58:42); immovable assets go to the State where located.
Ninth Schedule = government companies/corporations; Tenth Schedule = institutions with continued facilities.
Employee allocation between AP and Telangana was guided by the Kamalanathan Committee.
Section 46: 13th FC award apportioned; President to refer to 14th FC for separate awards.
Special development package to focus on Rayalaseema and north-coastal regions (s.46).
items.source: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (s.46, s.68-77, Ninth & Tenth Schedules); Kamalanathan Committee

items.title: Water Management & Polavaram (National Project)
items.body:
## River management (Section 85)

- The Act created the **Krishna River Management Board (KRMB)** and the **Godavari River Management Board (GRMB)** under the Union.
- **Headquarters:** **KRMB in Andhra Pradesh**, **GRMB in Telangana**; they function on the principles of the **Eleventh Schedule**.
- **Section 89:** the term of the **Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal (KWDT)** was extended. **Section 91:** both successor States replace the erstwhile State on the **Tungabhadra Board**, which monitors High Level Canal, Low Level Canal and Rajolibanda Diversion Scheme releases.

## Polavaram — Section 90

- The **Polavaram Irrigation Project** on the **Godavari** is **declared a national project**.
- The **Union takes control** of its regulation and development; **Telangana's consent is deemed given**; the **Central Government executes** the project and secures all clearances (environment, forest, R&R).
- **Pending issue:** in 2016 execution was handed to AP on a **reimbursement** basis; the **funding scope (2013-14 vs revised cost estimates)** and R&R remain an active AP-Centre dispute.
keyPoints: Section 85 created KRMB and GRMB; KRMB HQ in AP, GRMB HQ in Telangana.
Section 89 extended the Krishna Water Disputes Tribunal term; Eleventh Schedule sets Board principles.
Section 91: both States replace undivided AP on the Tungabhadra Board.
Section 90 declared the Polavaram Irrigation Project (on the Godavari) a national project.
Under s.90 the Union executes Polavaram and Telangana's consent is deemed given; funding remains disputed.
items.mnemonic: Boards swap sides: KRMB=AP, GRMB=Telangana (Krishna flows more to AP's core).
items.source: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (s.85, s.89, s.90, s.91, Eleventh Schedule)

items.title: Thirteenth Schedule Commitments, SCS Debate & Status (2026)
items.body:
## Thirteenth Schedule (s.93) — development commitments

- **Institutions for AP:** one each of **IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central University, Petroleum University, Agricultural University, IIIT**, an **AIIMS-type** super-specialty hospital-cum-teaching institution, a **Tribal University** and the **National Institute of Disaster Management**.
- **Infrastructure for AP:** a new **major port at Dugarajupatnam**; an **integrated steel plant in YSR (Kadapa) district**; a **Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC)** — India's first coastal economic corridor; a **new railway zone**; and upgrades to **Visakhapatnam, Vijayawada and Tirupati airports**.

## Special Category Status (SCS) vs Special Package

- **SCS was NOT part of the Act** — it was a **verbal assurance by the PM in the Rajya Sabha (Feb 2014)**.
- After the **14th FC** ended SCS for states other than NE/hill states, the Centre offered a **Special Package (Sept 2016)** with EAP-based funding in lieu of SCS. The SCS demand remains politically alive.

## Implementation status (as of 2026)

| Commitment | Status |
|---|---|
| Central institutions (IIT Tirupati, IIM Vizag, IISER Tirupati, Central Univ) | Largely established |
| New railway zone (South Coast Railway, HQ Visakhapatnam) | Sanctioned (2019) |
| Polavaram national project | Under execution; funding disputed |
| Dugarajupatnam port | Effectively dropped/unrealised |
| Kadapa steel plant | Scaled/partial, not completed as integrated SAIL plant |
| Special Category Status | Not granted |
keyPoints: Thirteenth Schedule promised AP an IIT, NIT, IIM, IISER, Central University, AIIMS-type institution and Tribal University.
AP infrastructure promises: Dugarajupatnam port, Kadapa (YSR) steel plant, VCIC corridor, a new railway zone, airport upgrades.
Special Category Status was a Rajya Sabha assurance (Feb 2014), not part of the Act.
14th FC ended SCS for most states; Centre offered a Special Package (2016) with EAP funding instead.
South Coast Railway zone (HQ Visakhapatnam) was sanctioned in 2019; Dugarajupatnam port and Kadapa steel plant remain unrealised.
items.source: AP Reorganisation Act 2014 (Thirteenth Schedule, s.93-94); Special Package 2016; Ministry of Railways (South Coast Railway zone, 2019)
